basis: COLLECTION.md §1, 'Sale consideration is not membership, and the acquirer leaves the base' (Erik, 2026-09-22, commit dafa302, ruled on these four rows). Intel Corporation reaches this base only through Greylock fund Section 16 filings, and the funds held that stock because Intel BOUGHT two Greylock companies: Shiva Corporation in 1998 and Xircom in 2001. Both are rows of their own here. The investment is Shiva and Xircom; Intel's own $503B scale is not Greylock's track record.

COLLECTION.md §1, 'Sale consideration is not membership, and the acquirer leaves the base' (Erik, 2026-09-22, commit dafa302, ruled on these four rows). UnitedHealth Group reaches this base only through the firm's own IPO roster, and the position behind it is Share Development, the HMO United HealthCare bought in 1985, which is a row of its own here. The firm's own surface carrying the acquirer does not make it a member; the investment is Share Development.

COLLECTION.md §1, 'Sale consideration is not membership, and the acquirer leaves the base' (Erik, 2026-09-22, commit dafa302, ruled on these four rows). 3Com reaches this base only through a fund filing dated 2001, years after 3Com bought Greylock's Sonix Communications in 1995. Sonix is a row of its own here. The investment is Sonix.

COLLECTION.md §1, 'Sale consideration is not membership, and the acquirer leaves the base' (Erik, 2026-09-22, commit dafa302, ruled on these four rows). Conexant Systems reaches this base only through a fund 13G dated 2001, the year after Conexant bought Greylock's Maker Communications in 2000. Maker Communications is a row of its own here.
